Theme

Civic life: news, government & the law

reform verb and noun

also reforms, reformer, reformed, political reform, amend, amendment

classical

Cic. Leg. 3.30: sīc ēmendārī et corrigī continentiā
Hor. Ep. 2.1.3: lēgibus ēmendēs
Traupman 157, 370

ēmendō, ēmendāre, ēmendāvī, ēmendātum

verb, first conjugation

reform, amend, correct

To free from faults (mendum, a fault): a state, laws, habits; its commonest use is correcting a text or a speech, and in Pliny the Elder curing a complaint (Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • corrigō, corrigere, corrēxī, corrēctum — set right, improve, reform

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Leg. 3.32: vel corrumpere mōrēs cīvitātis vel corrigere; Plaut. Trin. 1.2.81: ad frūgem corrigere (Lewis & Short)

    To make straight, and far more often to set right: a person, morals, a mistake; Cicero pairs it with ēmendāre (Lewis & Short).

  • ēmendātiō, ēmendātiōnis f. — a reform, an amendment, a correction

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Fin. 4.21: corrēctiō et ēmendātiō philosophiae veteris (Lewis & Short)

    The noun for a reform; corrēctiō is used beside it (Lewis & Short).

  • reformō, reformāre, reformāvī, reformātum — reshape; reform (a person, morals)

    verb, first conjugation · also used · post-classical · Sen. Ep. 25.1 (Lewis & Short); Plin. Pan. 53.1: mōrēs dēprāvātōs (Lewis & Short)

    Not before Augustus: first to reshape, transform (Ovid), then to reform a person or morals (Seneca, Pliny). Morgan–Owens records reformātiō agrāria for land reform, from a modern concordat.

Examples

  • cum tot sustineās et tanta negōtia sōlus, rēs Ītalās armīs tūtēris, mōribus ōrnēs, lēgibus ēmendēs

    since you alone carry so many and such great burdens, guarding Italy with arms, gracing her with morals, reforming her with lawsHor. Ep. 2.1.1–3

  • ut enim cupiditātibus prīncipum et vitiīs īnficī solet tōta cīvitās, sīc ēmendārī et corrigī continentiā

    for as a whole state is usually infected by the greed and vices of its leading men, so it is reformed and set right by their self-restraintCic. Leg. 3.30

See also legislation, correct, change, improve.
